luma-host-evt-7Iz2lapjAUQcL21.summaryLead: A recurring weekly AMA hosted by Superteam India where builders, founders, and investors share insights from the Solana ecosystem in an open conversation format.

sections.heading: What This AMA Is About
content: AMA with Atharv is Superteam India's weekly member-exclusive conversation series. Every Monday at 6:00 PM IST, the session brings together builders, founders, investors, and ecosystem contributors from across crypto for an informal discussion. The format is deliberately loose — think open conversation rather than structured keynote, with the host Atharv Velhal guiding the discussion and the community driving the questions.

Superteam itself is a global network focused on helping people learn, earn, and build on Solana. The India chapter has been running these AMAs as a regular touchpoint for the local community, creating a space where people can hear directly from the people shaping the ecosystem rather than reading secondhand summaries. Past attendees have included people from projects like Longshot Finance and others active in the Solana space, and the sessions regularly draw solid participation from the community.

What makes the series distinctive is its consistency. Running every single Monday without fail means the community builds a rhythm around it. People know where to show up, when to show up, and what kind of conversation to expect. That predictability is underrated in an industry where events tend to be sporadic and announcement-driven.

sections.heading: How the Sessions Run
content: Each AMA follows a similar arc: the guest shares what they're building, talks through lessons from their journey, and then opens up for questions from the Superteam India community. The emphasis is on real talk — mistakes, pivots, and hard-won insights rather than polished pitch decks. Because it happens on Google Meet, anyone with a registration can join from anywhere, though the timing is set for the Indian timezone.

The series repeats every Monday, which means you can drop in for a single session or make it a regular habit. If you catch one that resonates, you'll likely find the guest or host active on social media afterward, making it easy to follow up on anything that sparked your interest. The casual format also means you're just as likely to meet a fellow builder in the chat as you are to hear from the featured guest.

Hosts include Atharv Velhal alongside Paarug and the broader Superteam India team. The collaborative hosting approach means different perspectives shape the conversation, and the community feels ownership over the series rather than it being a one-person show. That shared ownership is part of what keeps people coming back week after week.

sections.heading: Why It Matters for Solana Builders
content: The Solana ecosystem moves fast, and events like this help cut through the noise. Instead of scanning Twitter threads or Telegram announcements, you get to hear directly from people who are knee-deep in the work. That proximity to builders is valuable whether you're evaluating a new protocol, looking for collaboration opportunities, or just trying to understand what's actually happening on-chain.

For anyone building on Solana or considering it, these AMAs are a low-commitment way to stay connected. There's no ticket price, no travel required, and the community aspect means you're not just consuming content — you're plugging into a network of people who are actively building. That network effect is often where the real value of events like this shows up, weeks or months after the call ends.

The fact that this particular session had 17 attendees marked as 'went' speaks to the engaged nature of the Superteam India community. In a space where many events struggle to attract consistent audiences, a weekly series that maintains participation is a sign that the format is meeting a real need.

luma-host-evt-uZcNvXgLxoQ26if.summaryLead: A virtual poker night hosted by Superteam India on Nomad Poker, pitting community members against each other for a 500 Devnet SOL prize pool.

sections.heading: The Concept Behind Poker Night
content: Superteam India Poker Night flips the typical crypto meetup format on its head. Instead of panels and presentations, you get a poker table. The event runs on Nomad Poker, a platform built for exactly this kind of community competition, and the stakes are real — at least in devnet terms. The prize pool is 500 SOL on devnet, which makes it a fun way to test your poker instincts without putting actual funds on the line.

The event is organized by the same crew behind the AMA with Atharv series, including hosts Atharv Velhal, Fahad Khan, Kshitij Gajapure, and Paarug. It's clearly designed as a social event first, with the competition aspect adding energy rather than intimidation. Superteam India describes the vibe as poker, competition, and community — a combination that works surprisingly well when everyone shares a professional interest in the same ecosystem.

The free pizza mention in the event description is a playful touch that nods to in-person poker culture. Even though this is a virtual event, the organizers are keeping the spirit alive by creating the feeling of sitting around a table with friends rather than staring at a screen in isolation.

sections.heading: Playing on Nomad Poker
content: Nomad Poker is the platform that makes this work. It's designed for crypto communities to host poker games, and the Superteam India event uses it to run what amounts to a private tournament. You can try the platform ahead of time at nomadpoker.fun to get comfortable with the interface before the actual event, which is a smart move for anyone who hasn't played online poker before.

The virtual format means anyone in the Superteam India community can join regardless of where they're physically located. Registration happens through the Luma event page, and once you're in, you'll be competing against fellow community members who share your interest in Solana and the broader crypto space. The barrier to entry is low, which is part of the appeal.

Devnet SOL as the prize currency is an interesting choice. It keeps the competition fun and accessible while still giving winners something to talk about. Nobody's risking their rent money, but the bragging rights are real. And in a community where reputation and connections matter, those bragging rights can translate into genuine social capital.

sections.heading: Community Building Through Cards
content: Events like this serve a dual purpose. On the surface, it's a fun way to spend an evening competing for bragging rights and a devnet prize pool. Underneath, it's a networking opportunity that doesn't feel like one. When you're playing cards with someone, conversations happen naturally, and you end up learning about what other people are building without the forced structure of a networking session.

The 19 people who showed up to the event represent a cross-section of the Superteam India community — builders, enthusiasts, and people who are just curious about what's happening in the Solana space. For a recurring community event, that kind of organic participation is a strong signal that the format works. It's the kind of thing that makes people come back, not for the poker, but for the connections they make at the table.

There's something to be said for events that don't take themselves too seriously. The crypto space is full of high-stakes conferences and intense hackathons. A poker night where the biggest risk is losing bragging rights provides a counterbalance to all that intensity, and the community is clearly responding to it.

luma-host-evt-nlLYpU09DZISw4E.summaryLead: An early morning group workout in Belgrade's Tašmajdan park during Belgrade Blockchain Week 2026, hosted by Wirex, CTRL community, Mighty Study, and Tangem.

sections.heading: What Happens at COW
content: Crypto Outdoor Workout — COW for short — is exactly what it sounds like: a group fitness session held outdoors, organized around major crypto conferences. The Belgrade edition takes place at Street gym in Tašmajdan park, starting at 6:00 AM. It's designed to be accessible to any fitness level, which means you can show up whether you're a seasoned athlete or someone who just wants to stretch before a long day of conference sessions.

The workout itself covers the fundamentals: warmup, squats, pushups, chin-ups, dips, abs, and stretches. There's also a pljeskavice thrown in — a playful reference to Serbian food culture that hints at the local flavor of this particular edition. Coaches are on hand to guide you through the movements, but you're also free to work out at your own pace, join or leave whenever you want, and generally treat it as a flexible start to the day.

The event is tagged under both Crypto and Fitness on Luma, capturing the dual nature of what's happening. It's not just a workout with a crypto label, and it's not just a crypto networking event held in a gym. It's genuinely both, appealing to people who want to move their bodies and meet people outside the usual exhibition hall setting.

sections.heading: The Sponsors and Their Roles
content: This edition is supported by four organizations, each bringing something different to the table. Wirex is the headline sponsor — a global payments platform that has been around since 2014 and has served over 7 million users across 130 countries. They've processed more than $20 billion in transactions and are a principal Visa and Mastercard member, which positions them at the intersection of crypto and traditional payments. For a workout event at a blockchain conference, that sponsorship makes sense.

CTRL is a non-profit community of open-source contributors, adding a developer-focused angle to the sponsorship. Tangem, a Swiss hardware wallet provider, brings the self-custody perspective — they've sold over 6 million card-shaped wallets that let users hold and manage thousands of coins offline without cables, batteries, or Bluetooth. ETHBelgrade, the Ethereum event happening in Belgrade during the same week, rounds out the support. The combination spans payments, open source, hardware, and the broader Ethereum community.

The diversity of sponsors reflects the cross-chain, cross-sector nature of the COW community. This isn't a single-protocol event; it's a gathering that welcomes anyone in the crypto space who wants to start their morning with physical activity and good company.

sections.heading: The Track Record and What Makes It Stick
content: COW has been running at crypto conferences for two years now, and the Belgrade edition is described as a return to where it all started. Previous editions have happened at Berlin Blockchain Week, EthCC in Cannes, Consensus Hong Kong, Devconnect Buenos Aires, Token2049 Singapore, and a dozen other events across Europe, Asia, and South America. That track record suggests the format fills a real need — conference attendees want a way to move their bodies and meet people outside the usual exhibition hall setting.

This particular session also comes with extras: drinking water, high-protein snacks, and limited edition merch. The organizers are clearly investing in making the experience worth showing up for, even at 6:00 AM. With 76 people registered for the Belgrade edition, it's one of the larger COW events, which makes sense given that Belgrade has become a significant hub for blockchain events in the Balkans.

The longevity of the COW series matters. When an event keeps showing up at conference after conference, it builds its own community of regulars. People plan their conference schedules around it, knowing they'll get a workout, some fresh air, and conversations with people they actually want to talk to. That kind of recurring, trusted event is rare in the crypto space, where everything tends to be new and untested.

luma-host-evt-c6CVoUpEc63KnuY.summaryLead: A weekly Wednesday evening gathering in Bangkok where founders, developers, and builders combine recovery sessions with genuine networking at ARAH ice bath and sauna facility.

sections.heading: The Wednesday Recovery Ritual
content: Founder Wellness & Networking Series is a weekly event organized by Superteam Thailand that runs every Wednesday evening in Bangkok. The concept is simple: founders and builders in tech, AI, and Web3 need a way to recharge midweek, and the organizers figured that combining wellness activities with networking would be more effective than another panel discussion. The result is an evening that starts with food and drinks and moves into a structured recovery circuit.

The timeline is straightforward. From 5:30 to 6:30 PM, attendees settle in with healthy food and drinks, reconnect with familiar faces, and make new introductions in a casual setting. From 6:30 to 8:30 PM, the focus shifts to the recovery circuit at ARAH, which includes sauna, ice bath, cold plunge, swimming pool access, and a candlelit recovery space. The entire experience costs 500 THB, which covers the recovery facilities.

The progression from social hour to recovery session is deliberate. By the time people hit the ice bath, they've already had real conversations with the people around them. That shared experience of cold water and heat therapy creates a bond that a cocktail hour alone can't replicate. It's wellness with a social purpose.

sections.heading: Breaking from the Usual Meetup Format
content: Superteam Thailand positions this explicitly against the traditional meetup format. No presentations, no panels, no endless pitching. Instead, the emphasis is on genuine conversations with some of Bangkok's most ambitious builders. The organizer behind it is OnlyFounders, working in partnership with Superteam Thailand to create something that feels more like a regular gathering of peers than a one-off event.

The audience includes founders, developers, designers, creators, investors, and operators. Whether you're actively building a startup or simply looking to meet ambitious people in Bangkok, you're welcome. The event is tagged under Tech and Wellness on Luma, and it's been featured in the Bangkok discovery section, which means it's getting visibility beyond just the Superteam Thailand community.

The sold-out status — 68 people registered — speaks to the demand for this kind of event in Bangkok. The city has become a major hub for Web3 builders and digital nomads, but the social scene often revolves around bars and loud venues. This provides an alternative that's both healthier and more conducive to actual conversation.

sections.heading: The Venue and Why It Works
content: ARAH is located at 88, 8 Sukhumvit 49 in the Khlong Tan Nuea area of Watthana, Bangkok. It's a dedicated facility for ice baths, saunas, and hot tubs — not a hotel wellness center or a repurposed gym. The specific address puts it in one of Bangkok's more accessible neighborhoods for the expat and tech community that tends to overlap with the Web3 scene.

For founders who spend their days staring at screens, managing teams, and making decisions under pressure, the recovery aspect isn't a gimmick. Cold plunges and sauna sessions have genuine benefits for stress reduction and mental clarity, and combining that with networking means you're investing in both your physical health and your professional network at the same time.

The weekly cadence is what makes this particularly valuable. One-off wellness events at conferences are nice, but they don't build habits. By running every Wednesday, Superteam Thailand is creating a ritual that founders can build their weeks around. The regularity means the community deepens over time, with people forming real relationships rather than collecting business cards at a single event.

luma-evt-6AOHAASiPKsinbz.summaryLead: The annual general assembly of DAO Suisse, covering governance review, elections, and strategic outlook at Dezentrum in Zürich.

sections.heading: The Formal Business at Hand
content: DAO Suisse General Assembly 2026 is the official annual meeting of DAO Suisse, a Swiss association operating in the crypto space. The event takes place on August 26 at Dezentrum in Zürich, running from 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM. It follows the standard structure of a Swiss association general assembly, with a clear agenda that covers the essentials: a recap of the organization's second year, the discharge and realignment process, elections, and the financial statement.

The formal portion runs from 5:00 PM to 6:15 PM, broken into five segments of 15 minutes each. After arrival and the recap of the second year, the assembly moves through discharge and realignment, elections and the financial statement, and concludes with an outlook on future initiatives. This is where the organization's governance gets exercised — motions, votes, and the kind of democratic process that gives associations their legitimacy.

Motions from association members had to be submitted at least 15 days before the assembly, which is standard governance practice for Swiss associations. This requirement ensures that proposals are reviewed and discussed before the actual meeting, keeping the assembly focused on decision-making rather than lengthy deliberation on new items.

sections.heading: Virtual and In-Person Participation
content: One practical detail that stands out: the assembly offers a virtual attendance option via Microsoft Teams. For an organization operating in the crypto space, this hybrid approach makes sense — not every member can travel to Zürich, but everyone should have the chance to participate in governance decisions. The Teams link is provided on the event page, making it straightforward to join remotely.

In-person attendees get the added benefit of the apéro that follows the formal business, starting at 6:15 PM. This is where the real community building happens — after the votes are cast and the financials are reviewed, members can connect over drinks and discuss what the assembly revealed about the organization's direction. The informal conversations at events like this often matter as much as the formal proceedings.

The venue, Dezentrum at Lessingstrasse 15 in the 8002 postal code of Zürich, is a known gathering spot in the city's crypto and tech community. Choosing a familiar venue reduces friction for attendees and signals that this is a community event, not a corporate function held in a sterile conference room.

sections.heading: Why This Assembly Matters
content: For members of DAO Suisse, this is the annual checkpoint where the organization's past year gets reviewed and its future gets shaped. The discharge process is where members approve or question how the board has managed the association, and the elections determine who will lead it going forward. The financial statement provides transparency into how resources have been allocated and whether the organization is on solid financial footing.

The timing is also notable. Coming in late August, the assembly sets the tone for the fall and winter programming. The outlook and future initiatives segment is where new directions get proposed, which makes it relevant not just for current members but for anyone considering getting involved with DAO Suisse. It's a window into what the organization plans to prioritize in the months ahead.

With 11 people registered to attend, it's a small but engaged group — the kind of setting where individual voices actually matter in governance decisions. In larger organizations, your vote gets diluted among thousands. At an assembly like this, each person's input carries weight. For anyone interested in how crypto-native organizations handle governance in practice, watching DAO Suisse operate is instructive.

luma-evt-XJRrcu8kmK4u3aN.summaryLead: A women-only event in Zürich exploring the intersection of relationships, personal finance, and Bitcoin, presented by SatoShe with therapist Ramona Zenger.

sections.heading: The Psychology Behind Money Conflicts
content: Liebe, Geld & Bitcoin — Love, Money & Bitcoin — tackles something most people avoid talking about: how couples handle finances. The event is structured around a simple premise that money is one of the most common sources of conflict in relationships and simultaneously one of the biggest taboos. SatoShe, a Bitcoin education organization focused on women, brings together two perspectives that complement each other: couples therapy and Bitcoin education.

The evening features Ramona Zenger, a couples and psychotherapist who has appeared on the Blick podcast 'intim&laut' and SRF's 'Deep Dating.' She'll explain why money conversations so often end in conflict and what's psychologically behind those patterns. Beyond the psychology, the event covers the financial reality of women in Switzerland — wage gaps, part-time work, care work, pension funds, and prenuptial agreements, all presented in an accessible way that doesn't require a finance background.

The combination of therapeutic expertise and financial education is unusual. Most crypto events focus purely on the technical or investment side of things. By starting with the psychological dynamics of money conversations, this event acknowledges that financial decisions don't happen in a vacuum — they happen within relationships, and those relationships have their own complexities.

sections.heading: Bitcoin as a Foundation for Long-Term Wealth
content: The Bitcoin portion of the evening is designed for people with no prior knowledge. It starts with a brief, accessible introduction to why the current monetary system pushes people to work and invest more, and how hard money changes that dynamic. From there, it moves into practical applications: building wealth for children, managing inheritance, and navigating the trust question around private keys in a partnership.

The event also addresses the social dynamics of introducing Bitcoin to a resistant or misinformed partner. This is a common friction point in relationships where one person is interested in crypto and the other isn't, and the session provides concrete strategies for handling those conversations without damaging the relationship. A scientifically grounded couple's exercise is included as a takeaway, designed to strengthen financial conversations at home.

By framing Bitcoin not as a speculative investment but as a tool for long-term financial planning, the event positions it as something that benefits the whole family. The inheritance and children angle is particularly compelling — it moves the conversation beyond portfolio allocation and into legacy building, which resonates differently than typical crypto pitch decks.

sections.heading: Practical Details and Who Should Attend
content: The event takes place at MME Legal | Tax | Compliance on Zollstrasse 62 in Zürich, a venue that signals legal and financial credibility. Doors open at 6:00 PM with the program starting at 6:15 PM, running until approximately 9:00 PM. Tickets are CHF 49, with a discounted rate of CHF 39 for SatoShe Circle members. An apéro is included in the ticket price.

The evening is explicitly labeled as ladies only, though it's open to all women regardless of relationship status. The format is interactive, starting with an open round and encouraging questions and experiences from attendees. SatoShe Circle members get additional benefits, including session credits for annual members. The event carries a disclaimer that it's for educational purposes only and does not constitute financial advice.

For women in Zürich who are curious about Bitcoin and want to understand how it fits into personal financial planning within a relationship, this is a rare combination of relationship advice and crypto education. The 17 people registered so far represent a mix of SatoShe Circle members and newcomers, which suggests the event is reaching both its core audience and people who are just getting started.
